structured_output.summary:
The tree has improved its noise model, but its mechanistic claims and node statuses have fallen behind its own data. Three problems stand out:

1. **The H2 'bytes over FLOPs' core rests on an accounting error.** It leaves out the group-2 conv1 dgrad that the late freeze also removes. With it counted, E116's 15-20% step saving is FLOP-proportional. E117 and E123 are FLOP-proportional too. E122's per-group attribution over-predicts E116's saving, so the profiler-based projections (including the group-2 freeze) are suspect.

2. **The tip still pays for unvalidated purchases.** E121 (99 seeds) shows that extra updates buy nothing, yet the bs-1024 late phases remain in the tip (~2.5% time) on 8-seed evidence. A 100-seed revert arm is the cheapest likely gain. Several nodes contradicted by results remain open or inconclusive: H10, H12.1.1 and H2.19.1.

3. **Every pp-per-1% verdict depends on a yardstick that was never measured.** The 32 px epoch slope has never been measured on the large-seed instrument, even though such runs take ~8 minutes. Meanwhile the biggest measured time levers sit untested for accuracy at low confidence: depth cuts at -7.6% and -6.1% (E123) and group-3 width 512 at -5.2% (E117). 12 px was retired against its own cost measurement.

The acceptance rule banked a tip (population mean 0.7521) that has passed the local gate 1 time in 6. Margin is gone, so every further cut has to be funded.

E124's -0.82 pp is far outside its predicted band and conflicts with E114. BN batch-stat correlation and a broken flip parity are more plausible explanations than 'coverage'.

Suggested order:
1. Free status and provenance cleanup.
2. A 100-seed arm reverting the late phases to bs 1536.
3. ±0.25 ep slope arms at 32 px.
4. 100-seed accuracy arms for the depth cuts and group-3 width 512.
5. Lookahead removal and the 12 px swap as cheap extras.
